comment: RATCHET BASELINE for check_uncalled_entry_points (ARC 034, sub-agent D).
THE PROPERTY: a public entry point defined in SHIPPED code with ZERO call
sites in SHIPPED code. `shipped` is every tracked *.py under scripts/ that
is NOT under scripts/tests/; checks/ is a GATE and is deliberately NOT
shipped, because a class whose only constructor in the tree is the check
that measures it is precisely the situation this detector exists to name.
WHY IT EXISTS. ARC 033 shipped the correlation-cap origin write built,
gated, and with zero production callers (CHECK-DEBT D3.150, D3.178) — it
was invisible until somebody asked. ARC 034's D3.191 audit then measured
the same class at 5x scale: five of six ARC 033 modules have zero
production importers and 170 of 176 public symbols have no production
caller. Every instrument in this tree asked whether code does the right
thing WHEN DRIVEN; none asked whether anything drives it.
THIS FILE MAY ONLY SHRINK. A finding not accepted here is a FAIL
(regression). An accepted entry that acquires a caller, or whose symbol no
longer exists, is also a FAIL (stale baseline), so this cannot rot into a
permanent suppression file. Any ADDITION relative to the tightest revision
ever COMMITTED must name the arc that admitted it in `admitted`, and that
revision is derived from this file's own git history — the one record the
edit under judgement cannot reach in the same motion.
IT IS NOT REGENERATED BY THE GATE. An instrument that rewrites its own
baseline manufactures its own green; check_uncalled_entry_points has
CORRECTABLE = False and no write path at all.
EVERY `owner` IS `unassigned`, AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER RATHER THAN A
PLACEHOLDER. Doctrine B.3: an owner that cannot pay is no owner wearing a
name. No arc has committed to wiring any of these entry points, and
writing `ARC 035` beside 194 findings would be furniture. The consequence
is deliberate and is not a defect in the gate: `unassigned` defers, so the
gate's day-one verdict is CANNOT_MEASURE — a withheld certification over a
measured backlog nobody owns — rather than a GUARDED that implies a
promise somebody made. Assigning owners is an architect decision; the
moment a module gets a live arc, that module stops deferring.
WHAT A GREEN HERE WOULD NOT PROVE, stated so it is never over-read:
dynamic dispatch (getattr, callable tables, dispatch through a string) is
INVISIBLE to a static reference walk, and a call SITE is not proof that
the site executes. See the gate's own docstring for the four named limits.

scripts/broker/broker_datafeed_ibkr.py.reason: The IBKR datafeed adapter. Its verbs are the BrokerDatafeedPort surface and the capture path that would call them (scripts/capture.py wiring a real vendor feed) is not built — the adapter is driven by scripts/tests/ and by the two datafeed gates only. This is the D3.10 asymmetry stated as an enumeration rather than as a sentence.

scripts/broker/broker_order_ibkr.py.reason: The IBKR order adapter. Same shape as its datafeed sibling: the order path verbs are reached by tests and by the seam simulation, and no shipped consumer constructs the adapter.

scripts/broker/broker_seam.py.reason: THE PORT DECLARATIONS. Almost every finding here is a Protocol verb or a declared capability on a port whose CONSUMER has not been built: the seam was authored ahead of the Limiter that reads it, which is the sequencing this project chose. The two Await*Divergent* doubles are deliberate plants kept in shipped code so check_await_conformance has a real divergence to find, and a plant with no production caller is what a plant is.

scripts/broker/ibkr_mapping.py.reason: The vendor mapping helpers. Reached by the two adapters for the shapes they use; these two entry points are the shapes nothing has needed yet.

scripts/capture.py.reason: The capture path. These verbs belong to the staleness monitor half, which the feed-kill drill and the tests drive; the daemon loop that would consult it on every tick is not wired.

scripts/crucible/calendar.py.reason: The Crucible calendar reader. Its roll and session helpers are consumed by nixrisk/roll.py and nixrisk/blackout.py for the shapes those modules use; these five are the query surface nothing has needed yet. D3.191 separately records that no check in the tree measures this file at all.

scripts/monitor.py.reason: The deprecated MON-1 monitor TUI. check_monitor was retired forward by ARC 030 / 1.2 and the tooling is not being extended, so these entry points are dead surface on a module the operator ruled is kept tracked and unowned.

scripts/nixalloc/caps.py.reason: The correlation-bucket cap. Driven by check_allocator_caps and by the sizing pathway for the verbs it uses; these two are the reporting surface no consumer reads.

scripts/nixalloc/contention.py.reason: Performance-weighted contention. The Allocator's own docstring records that the contention rank has no production wiring, which is what these three findings are as an enumeration.

scripts/nixalloc/lifecycle.py.reason: Strategy registration lifecycle. The R5 producer that would drive these transitions does not exist — CHECK-DEBT D3.155 already says the gate reflects a state whose producer is absent, and this is the same fact counted per entry point.

scripts/nixalloc/mirror.py.reason: The Limiter-side mirror consumer. One reporting verb, reached only by its own gate.

scripts/nixalloc/seam.py.reason: The frozen consumer-side seam. One declared verb with no consumer yet.

scripts/nixalloc/sizing.py.reason: The sizing pathway. One reporting verb no consumer reads.

scripts/nixalloc/wiring.py.reason: The Allocator's composition root. It is itself the thing that would be called at boot, and nothing boots the Allocator: these four are the top of a tree with no root above it.

scripts/nixbus/core_map.py.reason: The core map. Eight of nine are GATE-ONLY — the only non-test code that calls them is checks/check_core_map.py and checks/check_reserved_cores.py. That is exactly the ARC 033 shape this gate is named for, arriving from a different arc: the module is real, measured, and consumed by its own instrument and nothing else.

scripts/nixbus/price_ring.py.reason: The SPSC price ring. One reporting verb; the ring itself is driven.

scripts/nixbus/statebus.py.reason: The ipc:// state bus. Two verbs whose production consumer is the daemon loop that is not built.

scripts/nixrisk/blackout.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. BlackoutEvaluator satisfies gate.SymbolFlagPort and nothing in production constructs it or passes it to default_manifest — the producer was built behind a consumer that exists, and the two have never been joined. D3.191's cross-cutting result, per entry point.

scripts/nixrisk/calendar_seam.py.reason: The calendar/margin seam declarations. One declared verb with no consumer.

scripts/nixrisk/coldstart.py.reason: Cold-start reconciliation. Three of five are GATE-ONLY: check_coldstart is the only non-test caller. Nothing boots the Limiter, so nothing cold-starts it.

scripts/nixrisk/execution.py.reason: The execution ledger. Its query surface is read by check_execution_ledger and by tests; no shipped consumer reads a derived position back out.

scripts/nixrisk/freshness.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. SourceMonotonicGuard.keys and ClockSkewMonitor.latest are two of the four symbols D3.191 measured as referenced NOWHERE but their own definition. The module has exactly one importer in the tree (pollers.py), which itself has no production importer.

scripts/nixrisk/gate.py.reason: The two-phase gate pass. Its reporting surface is read by its own gate; the pass itself IS called from the seam.

scripts/nixrisk/halt.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. The HALT state machine: nine public verbs including replay_markers, the cold-start reconciliation §12.5:637 of docs/nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md names, with no production caller. The flag satisfies gate.HaltFlagPort and nothing in production constructs one, so branch 0 reads a port nobody produces.

scripts/nixrisk/outcomes.py.reason: §3's terminal handlers. These rows did not appear because anything regressed — they became MEASURABLE. Before ARC 046 nothing in shipped code constructed `OrderOutcomes`, so every verb on it was CANNOT-RESOLVE, which this gate reports and never counts. ARC 046 wired the daemon: `scripts/limiterd.py` constructs it and `scripts/nixrisk/completions.py` dispatches a §2A on_cancel to it, so `on_cancel` was CALLED and left this baseline in the same arc that revealed the rest. **ARC 053 SHRANK IT BY TWO, and both left for the reason the file says they would — their completion path was wired, not because anything here was edited to make room.** `on_reject` is now CALLED by `completions.py::CompletionDispatcher._dispatch_reject` (§2A's on_reject joined `WIRED_EVENTS`), and `resolve_pending_timeouts` is now CALLED by `limiterd.py::PendingTimeoutPoller.poll_due`, which the loop runs inside every tick. The ratchet moved in the ONE direction it is allowed to move. What remains is the observables: `history` and `released_margin` are read by a future arc's gate off those same paths, and each leaves when something reads it.

scripts/nixrisk/picture.py.reason: The financial-picture publisher. Two reporting verbs no consumer reads.

scripts/nixrisk/pollers.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. PushDemotion.last_push is one of the four symbols D3.191 measured as referenced nowhere but its own definition. ARC 034 repaired the MONOTONICITY defect behind it (D3.194) and deliberately did not delete the accessor: the repair is what a consumer will need to read.

scripts/nixrisk/positions.py.reason: PositionOriginWriter.on_fill is the ARC 033 origin write. ARC 047: `PositionOriginWriter.unstopped` LEFT this baseline — scripts/limiterd.py's FillPath.record() publishes it in the daemon's own status reply and stop record, so the unprotected-position escalation surface §14 names is now read by the process that can create one. `on_fill` itself has had a production caller since ARC 047 wired the §2A:75 fill completion into limiterd. CHECK-DEBT D3.150 and D3.178 are this row.

scripts/nixrisk/reservations.py.reason: The reservation ledger. ARC 046: `refusals` and `released` LEFT this baseline — scripts/limiterd.py's runtime/stop record now reads both, so the ledger's own audit surface is called by the process that owns it. The two remaining rows are the §11.7 full-scan reconcile, which still has no production caller.

scripts/nixrisk/roll.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. RollIdentityBook.next_roll_instant is one of the symbols D3.191 measured as answerable and unasked; five of seven are GATE-ONLY, reached only by checks/check_contract_roll.py. The roll epoch is published to nobody.

scripts/nixrisk/seam.py.reason: The frozen Limiter seam. Ten declared Protocol verbs with no consumer — these are contract declarations authored ahead of their producers, which is the sequencing, but a declared verb nothing consumes is still a declared verb nothing consumes.

scripts/nixrisk/session.py.reason: ARC 033 Stage 1. SessionFlattener.is_due has zero callers and tick_async re-implements its comparison inline; fired_outcome is written and never read. Both are named in the D3.191 audit as measured, and both survive here rather than being deleted, because the scheduler that should call is_due is the thing that is missing.

scripts/nixrisk/survival.py.reason: The survival watch. One verb, reached only by its own gate.

scripts/nixrisk/wal.py.reason: The Plane-1 write-ahead log. Three verbs whose consumer is the Limiter process that does not run.

scripts/nixverify/actuation.py.reason: Verify machinery. The actuation surface is exercised by every standalone check run and by scripts/tests/test_actuation.py; these three are the session-state and re-verification reporting verbs no check reads. NOTE the scope rule: checks/ is not shipped code, so a nixverify verb called only by a check is honestly GATE-ONLY here rather than hidden.

scripts/nixverify/contract.py.reason: Verify machinery. All four are GATE-ONLY by this gate's scope rule — the callers are checks/check_*.py, which are not shipped code. Recorded rather than excused: the point of the rule is that a gate calling a thing is not production wiring, and applying it to the verify family too is what keeps it a rule.

scripts/nixverify/declarations.py.reason: Verify machinery. One GATE-ONLY reader, called by checks/check_artifact_gate_coverage.py.

scripts/nixverify/observe.py.reason: Verify machinery. Three GATE-ONLY verbs, called by checks/check_observed_resource_claims.py.

scripts/nixverify/plane2.py.reason: Verify machinery. Three GATE-ONLY verbs on the journald handler, called by checks/check_verify_logging.py and checks/check_capture_plane2.py.

scripts/nixverify/render.py.reason: Verify machinery. Two presentation verbs no caller reaches; set_expected_durations in particular is a configuration hook nothing configures.

scripts/nixverify/venv_lock.py.reason: Verify machinery. Two GATE-ONLY verbs on the venv-mutation lock, called by the three venv checks.

scripts/risk_config.py.reason: The per-module config loader. These readers are the knobs no consumer has asked for yet — including session_flatten_lead_min, which D3.191 measured as never called by check_session_flatten either, so the lead time is hardcoded in the gate and read from config by nobody.
